text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Greek Foreign Minister Teodoros Pangalos and his Albanian counterpart Paskal Milo signed a protocol to issue temporary work permits to some 300,000 Albanian immigrants.
- Parliament elected the general council of state-run television, which will replace the executive director and his staff.

- The paper says that ex-Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi and former Democratic Party chairman Tritan Shehu were not part of a group organising the party congress, a clear sign that former president Sali Berisha has taken control of the party.
- An independent member of parliament says in an interview that the law banning communist party activity in Albania should be changed.
- Finance Minister Arben Malaj said that International Monetary Fund and the World Bank had worked out two special programmes to help Albania rebuild its shattered economy.
- Tirana police will start to remove hundreds of kiosks which were built over the past five years without any permit from the townhall.
- Vlore residents started to hand in weapons they had looted in the army depots during the rebellion in March.
- An editorial says the visit in Tirana of a Greek delegation headed by the foreign minister Teodors Pangalos shows that Athens, along with Rome, has economic and political interest in Albania.
- Main opposition Democratic Party called on civil servants not to yield to pressure from the Socialist-led coalition to resign so they can be replaced with its supporters.
- Two-page report on successful police action against criminal gangs across the country.
- The paper claims a criminal band from port town of Vlore left for a western country ahead of a major police operation to clear the town of several dangerous gangs.
- Official figures say one-fourth of the Albanian population is unemployed.
- Democratic Party leader Sali Berisha told visiting Greek Foreign Minister Teodor Pangalos that his party would return to parliament after a short period of boycott.
